protein: GB1 (B1 immunoglobulin-binding domain of streptococcal protein G)
readout: e_bind, IgG binding enrichment (log10), relative to wild-type GB1
assay_method: Yeast surface display with FACS and Illumina counting. GB1 designs codon-optimized for S. cerevisiae, synthesized as a Twist oligo pool, cloned into pCTCON2 by Golden Gate and displayed in EBY100; induced in SGCAA overnight at 20 degC, then ~3e6 cells stained overnight at 4 degC with 15 nM Alexa647-conjugated human IgG1 and 3 ug/ml Alexa488-conjugated anti-myc IgY in PBS/0.2% BSA. Cells were sorted on a FACS Aria II into an IgG-binding population (b) and a display-only population (d); plasmids from each sorted population and from the unsorted library were recovered and sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq6000 (2x150 bp). A design's count is the number of reads exactly matching its designed nucleotide sequence, and designs with fewer than 10 counts in the unsorted population were discarded. Each population's counts were converted to proportions p and the binding enrichment computed as e_bind,i = log10(p_b,i / p_d,i) - log10(p_b,wt / p_d,wt) (Eq. 1); the value used is the mean of two independent sorting replicates.
remark: Sequence is quoted from the three WT rows of Supplementary Dataset 1: UniProt P06654 228-282 carrying T228Q, preceded by an initiator Met at position 1 that the 165-nt synthesized insert does not encode, and every mutation is renumbered +1 because the paper numbers from that Gln with the Met excluded; the Aga2p-HA and myc fusion partners of the display construct are not included. 1950 seq_ids collapse to 1930 rows: the wild type and 18 of the 25 calibration genotypes were each built with two or three synonymous codon sequences and are averaged, the worst spread being 0.842 log10 (calibration_seq_2). Readout is the ebind column of Source Data sheet "Figure S8d" used as it stands (the workbook's sheet labels run one behind the Supplementary Information's, where this is Fig. S9d); the wild type reads 0.115 rather than the 0 its definition implies, because Eq. 1 references the pooled wild-type proportions while each synonymous wild-type sequence is counted separately, and no rebasing is applied. For 32 of the 41 EnsC 5-mutant designs the mutations column of Supplementary Dataset 1 contradicts the seq column of the same row; this file follows seq, to which the dna_seq column translates exactly in all 1965 rows, and derives every mutant from it. Not included: edisp from the same sheet, the clonal display and IgG-binding MFUs of Figure 5a and the four binned-sort enrichments of Figure S15, all of which are separate work items; the IgG titration of Figure 5b (4 designs); the binned binding categories of Figure 3e (per-model counts only, with no per-variant assignment); the predicted fit column of Supplementary Dataset 1 (not a measurement); and the Wu et al. and Olson et al. fitness landscapes the paper evaluates its models on, which were measured by others.

protein: Nb^traN (synthetic camelid-framework nanobody against the Escherichia coli conjugative pilus-tip protein TraN), displayed on the E. coli surface
source_organism: Synthetic VHH library on a camelid framework, displayed in Escherichia coli MG1655 dOmpW
readout: Conjugative score, log2 enrichment after one round of conjugation-based selection, referenced to wild-type Nb^traN
assay_method: Whole-cell selection coupling nanobody-antigen binding to type IV secretion. A single-site saturation library of the 14-residue CDR3 (AYPLDEIGSHDPHS, 14 x 19 = 266 variants) was synthesized on a programmable column (GenScript), cloned into the pDSG323 surface-display backbone and electroporated into E. coli MG1655 dompW (>30,000 colonies). Conjugative E. coli S17-1 expressing TraN and carrying a mobilizable gentamycin-resistance plasmid served as the donor and the display library as the recipient; both were grown to log phase, diluted to OD600 = 0.0025 (donor) and 0.005 (library) and co-cultured in LB with aTc for 6 h at 37 degC and 200 rpm, then plated on gentamycin plus chloramphenicol. A single round of bio-panning was performed. Nanobody CDR3 amplicons from the pre-selection (P0) and post-selection (P1) populations were counted by UMI-tagged high-throughput sequencing, and the conjugative score computed as log2(Mut_P1% / Mut_P0%) - log2(Wt_P1% / Wt_P0%).

protein: IL-6Rmb_original, the de novo designed three-helix miniprotein antagonist of the interleukin-6 receptor alpha (parent of IL-6Rmb6 and IL-6Rmb10)
source_organism: De novo design (Rosetta/RIFdock), displayed on Saccharomyces cerevisiae EBY-100
readout: ln(KD_parent / KD_variant) for binding IL-6R alpha; higher means tighter binding
assay_method: Yeast surface display with titration sorting and NGS, following the Cao et al. protocol the paper cites. Single-site saturation mutagenesis libraries (every residue to each of the other 19 amino acids) were built on the top initial design hits, transformed into EBY-100 by electroporation, grown in C-Trp-Ura and induced overnight in SGCAA. Cells were first sorted for display level on anti-c-Myc FITC, then incubated with the biotinylated target and stained with streptavidin-phycoerythrin plus anti-c-Myc FITC; PE/FITC double-positive cells were enriched over three rounds of binding selection including a titration series with target concentrations from 1 nM to 1000 nM (this scan spans 0.1-1000 nM in the deposited fit). Each round's sorted population was lysed, amplified and sequenced, and a per-variant KD confidence interval (kd_lb, kd_ub) was fitted from the counts across concentrations by the authors' statistical model.
remark: Readout recomputed from the deposited per-variant KD interval table (combined_affinity.sc on Zenodo 12797779), following the collapse_confidence_intervals = True path of the authors' own create_ssm_graphs.ipynb, which is the setting that notebook ships with and the one that produces the SSM maps of Supplementary Fig. 11: each row's interval is collapsed to a point KD by kd_center = sqrt(clip(kd_lb, lowest_conc/10, highest_conc*1e8) * clip(kd_ub, lowest_conc/10, highest_conc*1e8)), and the plotted effect reduces to ln(kd_center_parent / kd_center_variant). That is the quantity the paper describes as "the relative enrichment for each single mutant over the KD of its parent sequence"; it is already oriented so higher is tighter binding, and the wild-type row is 0 by construction. Rows the deposit marks low_conf are excluded, matching the grey cells of the published maps ("data too poor to estimate KD"); 35 of the 1083 designed variants are dropped this way, leaving 1048 of a complete 1083-variant scan (57 positions x 19). Sequence is the SSM parent from parent.list, byte-identical to IL-6Rmb_original in Supplementary Table 2. Phase 7: the paper builds IL-6Rmb10 by "combining the most enriched substitutions in the SSM", and its 8 substitutions land in the upper tail of this file - V47F is the single highest-scoring variant of all 1048 (+5.96), and S9V, E18R, R42L and L45Q all sit above the 94th percentile; K11E is one of the 35 low_conf rows and so is absent here. IL-6Rmb6 shares six of those and is scored the same way. Not included as separate work items: the SSM of the GP130 minibinder parent from the same deposit, whose parent KD falls below the lowest sorting concentration so that 56% of its variants collapse to exactly 0 (a censoring ceiling, not a measurement) - the paper itself abandons that map and picks GP130mb mutations from the combinatorial library instead; the initial-screen and combinatorial-library sorts of the same deposit, which are pools of distinct designs rather than variants of one sequence; and the BLI, SEC, CD, phospho-flow and organoid measurements, which cover a handful of purified designs.

protein: ATGL (PNPLA2), adipose triglyceride lipase; full-length, assayed as a Protein A-ATGL fusion
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt Q96AD5), expressed in HEK293T
readout: Co-immunoprecipitation log2 fold change for the interaction with CGI-58 (ABHD5), the ATGL co-activator; higher means more interaction retained
assay_method: LUMIER luminescence-based co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293T cells. Protein A was fused to the N-terminus of each ATGL variant, and the variants co-expressed with wild-type CGI-58 (ABHD5), the ATGL co-activator as a firefly-luciferase fusion. Lysates were immunoprecipitated in IgG-coated microtitre plates and the co-precipitated luciferase signal read out. Each value is the average log2 fold change of a triplicate experiment; the file uses the mean of the two independent assays (rep1, rep2) reported per variant.
remark: Readout is the mean of the CGI-58_rep1 and CGI-58_rep2 columns of Supplementary Data 4, taken as they stand. Sequence is UniProt Q96AD5 (human ATGL/PNPLA2, 504 aa) fetched whole; the label check passes with bad = 0 for all 52 mutant labels, and 504 matches the 504 positions of the Y2H scan in Source Data sheet SourceDataFig2A. The wild-type row is the measured "ATGL WT" row of the same table, not a definitional value. Phase 7: the paper names 11 partner-specific "switch" variants, and each lands near the strongest binding loss for its own partner in these files - for G0S2, N39E and L102K are ranks 1 and 2 of 52; for PLIN1, L178A and P103K are ranks 2 and 3 and A104E rank 6; for PLIN5, P86K and I70A are ranks 2 and 3, matching the statement that "the strongest reduction in binding of Plin5 was observed with the I70A, P86K, and L159A ATGL variants"; for CGI-58, R351L and F348E are ranks 5 and 6. The one variant that outranks them in three of the five files, G189E, is in the bottom five for every partner, which is why the paper classes it as globally disruptive rather than a switch. The 52 variants are the set the paper prioritised out of its Y2H scan for individual co-IP assessment (Supplementary Data 3); the five partners were assayed in the same experiment on the same plate, so they are five separate work items sharing one variant set and are curated as five files. Not included as separate work items: the upstream Y2H deep mutational interaction scan itself (Source Data sheet SourceDataFig2A), whose per-variant value is a count of how many times a codon was called significantly enriched, running 0 to 4 with 75-85% of cells at 0 - an enrichment-call tally rather than a graded measurement; the in vitro triglyceride hydrolase activity and cellular lipolysis assays of Figs. 4-5, which cover the 11 switch variants; and the lipid-droplet counts of Supplementary Data 5 (13 variants).

protein: 43829, a de novo designed mini-protein binder against the first receptor binding interface (RBI-1) of Clostridioides difficile toxin B
source_organism: De novo design (Rosetta/RIF docking), displayed on Saccharomyces cerevisiae
readout: WT-normalised log2 enrichment after one round of FACS sorting against TcdB2; higher means more enriched, i.e. better binding
assay_method: Yeast surface display with FACS sorting and NGS. A site-saturation mutagenesis library in which every residue of the 43829 minibinder was substituted with each of the 20 amino acids was displayed on yeast and sorted against biotinylated TcdB2 residues 1285-1804, the class II receptor binding interface 1. The unsorted library (R0) and the round-1 sorted population were deep sequenced, and the deposited processing pipeline reports, for every observed protein sequence, its read count and its frequency within that sample.
remark: Readout recomputed from the processed sorting counts deposited on figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.26562841, calculated.zip), which the paper names as the home of its processed high-throughput sequencing data. Each file lists a protein sequence, a read count and that count over the sample total; the enrichment used here is log2(freq_R1 / freq_R0) minus the same quantity for the 43829 parent, so the wild-type row is 0 by construction and higher means more enriched under selection - the same construction the deposit's own frequency column invites. Sequence is 43829 as printed in Supplementary Table 3 (65 aa) and is the first line of the R0 file. Two independent checks fix it: the six residues the paper mutates to alanine to map the interface, K5, F8, F9, W11, F12 and R16, sit exactly where those labels put them; and the R0 file contains exactly 1235 distinct single mutants, which is 65 x 19, so the designed library is complete and the numbering is 1-based on this sequence. Only variants observed in both R0 and the sorted pool are scored - 868 of the 1235 for this target. A variant present in R0 but absent after sorting is strongly depleted rather than unmeasured, but its zero count leaves the log ratio undefined, so it is excluded rather than floored. Phase 7: the paper reports that after sorting "residues at the binding interface and protein core were mostly conserved in both TcdB2 and TcdB4 samples". In this file the six interface residues named above are all far below the library as a whole - position means -4.79 (K5), -6.97 (F8), -6.30 (F9), -7.81 (W11), -5.82 (F12) and -7.56 (R16) against a whole-library mean of -3.90. The substitutions the paper carried from this scan into its evolved binders H1 and H3 sit in the enriched tail: N1F, shared by both, ranks 84th of 868, and T54I, the second substitution of H1, 128th. Not included as separate work items: the later TcdB2 sorting rounds R2-R5 of the same deposit, which are successive rounds of this one selection rather than parallel conditions and collapse as they go (R2 retains 470 single mutants, and by R4 the parent itself is absent, 0 reads, so the readout is no longer graded); the combinatorial library sorts (TcdB_combo R3-R6, up to 699 multi-mutants of 43829), for which no unsorted R0 sample is deposited, so no enrichment can be computed; the TcdB route1 and route2 sorts, which screen the initial pool of distinct designed minibinders rather than variants of one sequence; and the cryo-EM, BLI, cell-rounding and mouse colon-loop experiments of Figs. 2-6.

protein: GRB2 (growth factor receptor-bound protein 2), assayed as its C-terminal SH3 domain
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P62993), expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
readout: BindingPCA growth fitness for the GRB2-SH3 / GAB2 interaction, the log ratio of variant frequency after and before methotrexate selection, scaled so that the unmutated protein is 0; higher means tighter binding
assay_method: BindingPCA in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The protein of interest and its ligand (the GAB2 peptide) carry complementary fragments of a split murine dihydrofolate reductase, so the reconstituted enzyme - and hence methotrexate resistance - reports on the interaction rather than on abundance alone. A library of variants competes in a pooled culture for 5 generations and each variant's frequency before and after selection is read by sequencing; fitness is the log ratio, in triplicate.
remark: Sequence is UniProt P62993 (GRB2, 217 aa) fetched whole. Supplementary Table 4 gives each variant only as the mutated window, not the whole protein; the wild-type window occurs exactly once in the reference sequence, at residues 168-189, and mutant positions here are that offset applied. The assayed construct is not the full-length protein: it is the isolated C-terminal SH3 domain of GRB2 (UniProt annotates it as residues 156-215) fused to a dihydrofolate-reductase fragment for the protein-fragment complementation assay, and only residues 168-189 were mutated. The full-length reference is used as the sequence so that positions are canonical; residues outside the window rest on provenance alone. This dataset is library 3, all combinations of 15 single substitutions with mild fitness effects within a 22-residue window (2^15 designed), measured by BindingPCA. Readout is the "fitness" column of Supplementary Table 4, used as it stands; higher is already better, and the WT row is the table's own row flagged WT=TRUE. The variants are combinatorial, most carrying many substitutions at once, which is the point of the paper; multi-site genotypes are joined with ":". Phase 7: the mutant codes parsed out of the deposited windows reproduce each library's stated design exactly - library 1 uses 34 distinct single substitutions at 34 sites ("the largest set of mutations predicted to preserve both molecular phenotypes consisted of 34 single aa substitutions"), library 2 uses 4 sites with 76 = 4 x 19 distinct singles ("all possible substitutions at 4 physically interacting sites", 20^4), and libraries 3 and 4 each use exactly 15 distinct singles with genotypes up to 14 and 15 mutations deep (2^15 = 32,768 designed). Not included: the "1_lenient" rows of Supplementary Table 4, which are the same library 1 AbundancePCA experiment under a more permissive confidence filter (129,320 rows rather than 71,233) and would duplicate this dataset; the inferred folding and binding free energies of Supplementary Table 5, which are model output rather than measurement; the growthrate columns, which are the same measurement on another scale; and the shallow double-mutant ddPCA data for GRB2-SH3 and PSD95-PDZ3, which belong to an earlier publication (doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04586-4).
